subject: Culture
title: Seating Order Politics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Seating Order Politics.

hook.text: At a Chinese banquet, the guest of honor sits facing the door. It's not random—it's protocol.

buildup.text: Seating order reveals power. In medieval Europe, proximity to the king determined your status.

discovery.text: The phrase 'above the salt' comes from when the salt cellar separated nobles from commoners at the table.

twist.text: In egalitarian Scandinavian cultures, assigned seating feels forced. Everyone mixes freely.

climax.text: Where you sit at the table can honor you, test you, or put you in your place.

punchline.text: The chair is a political statement.

quiz.question: What did the phrase 'above the salt' originally indicate?
options: Higher social status at the table
